orchestration_result.query: Which tech stocks should I include in my bond portfolio?

bonds.analysis: Including tech stocks in a bond portfolio would violate the investment-grade only and fixed-income allocation constraints. The portfolio should consist of bonds with minimum credit ratings of BBB+ (S&P) or Baa1 (Moody's) and should focus on providing stability, predictable cash flows, and capital preservation. Tech stocks are equity investments and do not align with the fixed-income intent scope. Instead, consider investing in high-quality corporate bonds issued by tech companies if they meet the credit rating criteria. A laddered maturity structure will still be maintained, with no more than 30% of the portfolio maturing in any single year to ensure a steady cash flow and manage interest rate risk.

Allocate 40% to bonds, 35% to equities, and 25% to materials.
